subject: Private observability audit bridge - PoC & scope
messages:
From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>
To: secops@acme.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private observability audit bridge - PoC & scope

Hi Tom / Acme SecOps team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, we'd like to run a short PoC to validate an "audit bridge" pattern for private Redwood deployments in your VPC (on-prem equivalent if you prefer). The goals are:

- Demonstrate reliable delivery of logs/traces/metrics from the private deployment to your SIEM without routing customer data through our public control plane.
- Prove authn/authz model for forwarder (mTLS vs signed ephemeral tokens).
- Validate evidentiary chain/custody for compliance (timestamps, signed manifests, retention).

Proposed scope for PoC (2 weeks):
1) Deploy a lightweight forwarder inside a staging subnet that can emit: syslog (UDP/TCP), Splunk HEC, and a gzipped evidence bundle (S3-compatible presigned upload to your enclave).
2) Wire a tracing hook that forwards OTLP traces over mTLS to your trace intake for correlation.
3) Produce an evidence mapping CSV and a short runbook for ingestion + custody verification.

Questions for you before we kick off:
- Confirm allowed outbound destinations/ports from the staging subnet (we expect TCP 443 for HEC, optional UDP 514 for legacy syslog).
- Do you have a preference for authentication: client mTLS (preferred on our side) or per-request signed tokens?
- Acceptance criteria: what does "validated" look like from your SOC perspective? (we can propose a checklist).

I've attached a short spec that outlines the forwarder behavior and sample manifest formats.

If the above looks good, we'd like to schedule a short kickoff (30m) next week and deploy Monday after.

Thanks,
Hiro
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
hiro.tanaka@redwood.com
Attachment: audit-forwarder-spec-v1.pdf (spec stub, 120KB)

From: Tom Baker <tom.baker@acme.com>
To: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>
Cc: secops@acme.com
Date: Wed, 29 Oct 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private observability audit bridge - PoC & scope

Hiro,

Thanks — this is exactly the kind of thing we want to validate. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- Ports/destinations: We prefer TCP 514/1514 for syslog over TLS where possible, and Splunk HEC on 443. We can also accept OTLP over 4317 but that needs to be in a dedicated intake with mTLS.
- Authentication: our security team prefers client mTLS for the ingestion plane; signed tokens are acceptable for short-lived testing but not for final acceptance.
- Evidence custody: we need signed manifests (SHA256) and a delivery receipt with server-side timestamps.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Forwarder can deliver sample syslog and HEC payloads with end-to-end verification.
- Trace spans contain the instrumentation ID so we can correlate across Redwood-generated spans and our platform.
- Proof of custody: signed and verifiable artifacts with retention metadata.

I can provision a staging intake and provide firewall rules — see below (example):
- Allow outbound to 10.12.33.45:443 (HEC)
- Allow outbound to 10.12.33.46:1514 (syslog-tls)
- Allow outbound to 10.12.33.47:4317 (OTLP-mTLS)

I'll need an updated runbook and the exact certificate subject CN you plan to use for the mTLS client certs so we can whitelist.

Tom
Tom Baker | SecOps Engineer, Acme Corp
secops@acme.com

To: Tom Baker <tom.baker@acme.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Oct 2025 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private observability audit bridge - PoC & scope

Tom — thanks for the quick reply and the sample firewall rules. Answers inline and a few action items below.

- Ports/destinations: confirmed — we'll target HEC on 10.12.33.45:443, syslog-tls on 1514, and OTLP-mTLS on 4317. Forwarder will attempt TLS-first for syslog.
- Authentication: we'll plan to use client mTLS for the final PoC. For the initial smoke test we can spin up a signed token flow to speed things up; cert generation for mTLS will be scheduled before the acceptance run.
- Evidence custody: forwarder will produce a gzipped bundle (named evidence-<timestamp>.tar.gz) containing: logs/, traces.jsonl, manifest.json (SHA256 manifest), and delivery_receipt.txt which we will request from your intake.

Action items for Redwood: 
1) Share exact CN for client certs we will provision. (kimberly, can you take this?)
2) Provide a short runbook and the sample evidence bundle. (marissa, I attached the first cut spec; will you build the runbook?)
3) Schedule kickoff — propose Mon Nov 3, 10:00AM PT.

Attachments: audit-forwarder-spec-v1.pdf (copy included).

kimberly_park, marissa_cole — assigning offline tasks above.

—
Hiro
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
hiro.tanaka@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Baker <tom.baker@acme.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private observability audit bridge - PoC & scope

Tom / team,

Attached is the PoC runbook (poC-runbook-2025-11-03.md) and a sample evidence bundle we used in internal testing (sample-syslog-bundle.tar.gz). The runbook includes:

- Prep steps and terraform snippet to launch the forwarder in a staging subnet.
- Certificate provisioning flow and CN format (we used CN=redwood-forwarder.staging.redwood.example).
- Validation checklist (HEC success, syslog TLS handshake, OTLP trace delivery + span correlation).
- How to request the delivery_receipt from your intake (curl examples included).

Quick notes:
- We implemented HEC retries with idempotency keys in the header to avoid duplicate ingestion.
- Evidence manifest is a newline-delimited JSON with SHA256 entries for each file.

Please review and let us know if the CN above is acceptable for whitelisting. If that works, we will provision certs and perform the smoke test on Monday.

Attachments: poC-runbook-2025-11-03.md (8KB), sample-syslog-bundle.tar.gz (stub, 2MB)

Thanks,
Marissa
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Tom Baker <tom.baker@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>
Cc: secops@acme.com
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private observability audit bridge - PoC & scope

Marissa, Hiro,

This looks good. The CN format is acceptable — we'll whitelist CN=redwood-forwarder.staging.redwood.example for the staging intake. A few minor acceptance items from SOC:

- Ensure the signed manifest includes a UTC ISO8601 timestamp.
- Delivery receipt should contain receipt_id and server_timestamp and be signed by our intake cert.
- Retention: staging data will be kept for 30 days; production evidence retention policy will be defined during the procurement step.

Firewall rules confirmed (we've opened the three destinations you requested). Kickoff at Mon Nov 3 10:00AM PT worked for our engineers — however I'll note we performed a quick smoke today and saw OTLP spans arrive but without the instrumentation_id. Could you ensure the forwarder preserves the original span attributes and adds a redwood.forwarder_id tag for correlation?

Once we validate the manifest and receipts in the PoC, we'll capture the acceptance checklist and sign off from SOC.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.
Tom
SecOps Engineer | Acme Corp
secops@acme.com
